title: Investing in a Library of Experiences
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article ranks the three classic levers of talent development — learning best practices, undergoing assessment, and accumulating experience — and argues experience is the most powerful of the three, citing how seasoned leaders consistently point to specific experiences (not training courses) as the source of their growth. The piece highlights 'crucible' experiences like job rotation, crisis management, or leading in an unfamiliar culture as reshaping a leader's self-identity, and notes that many valuable experiences (community board service, coaching youth) sit outside the organization and cost little. It closes by urging organizations to deliberately curate an 'experience library' rather than leaving developmental experiences to chance.
points: Of the three main levers for talent development — best practice, assessment, and experience — the author argues experience has the most outsized influence on how leaders actually grow.
Transformative 'crucible' experiences (job rotation, leading in a new culture, crisis management) reshape a leader's self-identity, not just their skill set.
Many of the most powerful developmental experiences (coaching youth, serving on a board, spearheading a charity effort) exist outside the organization and cost little beyond time.
Great organizations deliberately curate an 'experience library' leaders can draw from at different career stages, rather than leaving growth experiences to chance.
quotes: When it comes to talent development, three essential investments stand out for their impact: best practice, assessment, and experience.
As important as best practice and assessment are to improvement, it is experience that has the most oversized influence on professional growth and development.
Experiences, both planned and unplanned, shape how leaders view the world, themselves, and their leadership.
Like other “crucible” experiences, they force leaders to confront uncertainty and adapt in a dynamic environment.
Leaving the experiences a leader encounters up to chance is just too risky. A runway full of curated experiences provides the lift leaders need to reach the highest altitudes.
